findings.issue: Pagination math (parseInt on ?page, NaN fallback, clamping to totalPages, slice bounds, 'Page n of total' text, pageUrl omitting page=1 at index.ts:20-35) is completely untested
findings.suggestion: Extract the page-clamp/slice logic into a pure function and unit-test edge cases: page=0, negative, non-numeric, page beyond totalPages, empty result set

findings.issue: pokemon→species mapping (deoxys-normal→deoxys), dedupe by speciesId, alternate-form exclusion and dex-order sort have no tests; a failed per-Pokémon fetch (.catch(() => null)) silently drops a card, making the '<count> Pokémon' text wrong
findings.suggestion: Unit-test speciesCards with fixture entries covering alternate forms, duplicate species, mixed entry shapes ({pokemon:{}} vs bare refs) and a rejected fetch

findings.issue: The whole sort comparator — missing-values-last in both directions, numeric vs localeCompare via data-n/data-v attributes, direction flipping via aria-sort — lives only in the browser and is untested; correctness depends on the template emitting data-v/data-n/data-missing ([name].ts:70-78,95-113), so a template refactor breaks sorting with no signal
findings.suggestion: Extract the row comparator as a pure function taking cell descriptors, and test missing-last in asc and desc, numeric columns, and string columns; note Type currently sorts by API name, not the English label shown

findings.issue: Filter pipeline untested: type filter uses the id≤10000 proxy for 'default Pokémon', generation filter by species-name set, search on humanized lowercase names; API errors are swallowed into species=[] (catch → 'No Pokémon found')
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the filter intersection with fixtures; distinguish API failure (500 or retry) from a genuinely empty result

findings.issue: Hand-rolled concurrency semaphore (acquire/release with a waiter queue) and promise cache with rejection-eviction are untested; the acquire/release accounting is exactly the kind of code that deadlocks or double-counts after a small edit
findings.suggestion: Add a test that runs >MAX_CONCURRENT fetches and asserts max observed in-flight count and that all resolve; test that a rejected api() call is not cached as permanently rejected

findings.issue: Move-table assembly untested: default game = highest order (selectedGame via .at(-1)), grouping by learn method, level-up sort by level-then-name, METHOD_ORDER comparator with its ai/bi -1 handling
findings.suggestion: Unit-test method ordering incl. a method not in METHOD_ORDER, and the level-up tie-break

findings.issue: Any API error — including a transient network failure — is rendered as 'Not found' with status 404; the not-found path and the error path are conflated and untested
findings.suggestion: Branch on ApiError.status (404 vs other) and test both paths

findings.issue: Pure, cheap-to-test helpers (humanize, dexNumber, latestFlavorText's reverse scan and \s+ collapse, englishName fallback, orMissing) are untested
findings.suggestion: A small vitest suite over table-driven fixtures; latestFlavorText's 'last English entry' semantics is the likeliest quiet break

findings.issue: URL-state handling (param omission for empty values, page reset on filter change, 250ms debounce) has no app-level tests; only the acceptance suite touches it
findings.suggestion: Add a Playwright component/route test for navigate(): setting a filter drops page, clearing q removes the param

findings.issue: Derived formatting untested: height/weight (x/10).toFixed(1), stat total reduce, stat-bar width percentages
findings.suggestion: Snapshot or assert the dl text and Total row for a fixture Pokémon

summary: The app ships with zero tests of its own: no runner, no test script, no test files. All correctness currently rests on the external acceptance suite, which will not run in day-to-day development; the riskiest logic (pagination, filtering, species mapping, DOM sorting, the hand-rolled fetch semaphore) is exactly the kind that breaks silently under refactor. The pure helpers in format.ts and species-cards.ts would be cheap to cover with vitest, and the client sort comparator should be extracted and tested before anyone touches the moves tables.
